title: LATE-INNING SURGE: Hurricanes rally past Eagles with decisive sixth-inning push - NewsBreak
text:
By J.W. COOKE Keys ,
5 hours ago
Breaking a 4-4 tie with a two-run sixth inning and capitalizing on late control issues, the Coral Shores High baseball team rallied past Master’s Academy 7-4 on Tuesday, March 24, at Founders Park.
Locked even entering the bottom of the sixth, Coral Shores took advantage without putting a ball in play, drawing a bases-loaded walk from Mailon Aguila to push across the go-ahead run before a hit batter forced in another for a three-run cushion.
Jumping ahead early, the Hurricanes scored twice in the first inning, using a Master’s Academy error and an RBI double to left by Riley O’Berry to build a quick 2-0 lead.
Answering in the third, Master’s Academy moved in front 3-2 behind an RBI single from Luke Alford, a bases-loaded walk by Chase Bell, and a Coral Shores error.
Responding again in the fifth, Coral Shores regained the lead when Maykol Bonito lifted a sacrifice fly, and Brayden Turner followed with an RBI single to center, making it 4-3.
Pulling even once more, Master’s Academy tied the game in the sixth on a two-strike single from Landon Alford, setting the stage for the Hurricanes’ decisive half-inning.
Starting on the mound, O’Berry allowed three runs — none earned — on three hits over three innings while striking out four. Chris Horowitz added a scoreless inning in relief to close it out.
Setting the tone offensively, Keller Blackburn went 2 for 4 with three runs scored and three stolen bases as part of a five-steal effort for Coral Shores, which also turned a double play.
Driving in runs, O’Berry, Bonito, and Turner each contributed an RBI as the Hurricanes finished with seven runs on seven hits.
Drawing eight walks, Master’s Academy showed patience at the plate but was undone by a key error and the sixth-inning rally.
Returning to action Thursday, Coral Shores will host Archbishop Carroll, looking to build on the comeback victory.
